question: A 10 kg block rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction between the block and the floor are 0.4 and 0.3. A horizontal force of 50 N is applied to the block. At t = 1 s after the force is applied, find the acceleration of the block, the friction force on it, and the normal force on it.

I'm pushing a 10 kg box along the floor with a steady 50 N horizontal shove. The floor has mu_s = 0.4 and mu_k = 0.3. One second in, what's the box's acceleration, the friction force on it, and the normal force?
10 kg block, floor mu_s 0.4 mu_k 0.3, horizontal push 50 N. At t = 1 s: acceleration, friction force, normal force.

A 5 kg block is released from rest at the top of a frictionless incline that makes an angle of 30 degrees with the horizontal and is 2 m long. At the instant of release, what are the block's acceleration and the normal force on it? How long does the block take to reach the bottom edge of the incline?

Say I let go of a 5 kg block at the top of a slick, frictionless 30 degree ramp that's 2 m long. Right when I let go, what's its acceleration and what's the normal force on it? And how long until it gets to the bottom edge?
5 kg block, top of frictionless ramp, 30 deg, length 2 m, released from rest. At t = 0: acceleration and normal force. Time to reach the edge?

A 5 kg block is released from rest at the top of a 3 m long incline inclined at 40 degrees to the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the incline is 0.5 and the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.4. At t = 0.5 s after release, determine the acceleration of the block, the friction force on it, and the normal force on it.

There's a 5 kg block sitting at the top of a 3 m ramp tilted at 40 degrees, and I let go of it. The ramp has mu_s = 0.5 and mu_k = 0.4. Half a second later, what's the block's acceleration, the friction force, and the normal force on it?
5 kg block at top of 40 deg incline, length 3 m, mu_s 0.5, mu_k 0.4, released from rest. At t = 0.5 s: acceleration, friction force, normal force.

A 5 kg block is placed at the top of a 4 m long incline inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal and released from rest. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction are 0.6 and 0.4. At t = 1 s, find the acceleration of the block and the friction force acting on it. Also find the minimum coefficient of static friction needed to keep the block from sliding.

I put a 5 kg block at the top of a 4 m long ramp tilted 30 degrees and let go. mu_s is 0.6 and mu_k is 0.4. After 1 second, what's its acceleration and the friction force on it? Also, what's the smallest mu_s that would stop it from sliding?
5 kg block, top of 30 deg incline, length 4 m, mu_s 0.6, mu_k 0.4, released from rest. At t = 1 s: acceleration, friction force. Minimum mu_s to keep it from sliding?

A 0.5 kg ball is thrown from the origin with a horizontal velocity component of 10 m/s and a vertical velocity component of 10 m/s upward. Neglecting air resistance, find the position and the velocity of the ball at t = 2 s.
I throw a 0.5 kg ball from the origin so it's moving 10 m/s sideways and 10 m/s upward. No air resistance. Where is it and how fast is it going (velocity) after 2 seconds?
0.5 kg ball thrown from origin, vx = 10 m/s, vy = 10 m/s up, no drag. Position and velocity at t = 2 s.

A 2 kg block moves at an initial speed of 10 m/s along a horizontal floor. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction between the block and the floor are 0.6 and 0.5. Find the time at which the block comes to rest, the distance it travels, and the total work done on the block between t = 0 and t = 6 s.

A 2 kg block is moving along the floor at 10 m/s, and the floor has mu_s = 0.6, mu_k = 0.5. When does it come to a stop, how far does it go, and what's the total work done on it from t = 0 to t = 6 s?
2 kg block moving at 10 m/s on a floor, mu_s 0.6, mu_k 0.5. Stop time, distance travelled, work done on block t = 0 to 6 s.

A 4 kg block rests on a frictionless horizontal floor and is attached to a fixed wall by a spring with spring constant 100 N/m. The spring is stretched by 0.5 m from its natural length and the block is released from rest. Find the position and the velocity of the block at t = 5 s.

A 4 kg block sits on a frictionless floor, hooked to a wall with a 100 N/m spring. I pull it out so the spring is stretched 0.5 m, then let go. Where is the block and what's its velocity 5 seconds later?
4 kg block, frictionless floor, spring k = 100 N/m fixed to wall, stretched 0.5 m then released from rest. Position and velocity at t = 5 s.

Two masses of 3 kg and 5 kg are connected by a light string passing over a frictionless, massless pulley. The system is released from rest. At t = 0.2 s, find the acceleration of each mass and the tension in the string.
I've got a 3 kg mass and a 5 kg mass tied together with a string over an ideal pulley, and I let go from rest. 0.2 seconds in, what's the acceleration of each mass and the tension in the string?
Atwood machine, 3 kg and 5 kg, ideal pulley and string, released from rest. At t = 0.2 s: acceleration of each mass, string tension.

A 4 kg block rests on a horizontal table, 1 m above the floor, and is connected by a light string over a frictionless pulley at the table edge to a 6 kg block hanging 0.5 m above the floor. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction for all surfaces are 0.3 and 0.2. The system is released from rest. At t = 0.2 s, find the acceleration of the 4 kg block and the tension in the string. Also find when the string goes slack and when the 4 kg block comes to rest.

A 4 kg block sits on a table 1 m off the floor and is tied over a pulley at the edge to a 6 kg block hanging 0.5 m above the floor. All surfaces have mu_s = 0.3 and mu_k = 0.2. I release everything from rest. At 0.2 s, what's the 4 kg block's acceleration and the string tension? When does the string go slack, and when does the 4 kg block stop?

4 kg block on table (1 m high), string over edge pulley to 6 kg block 0.5 m above floor, all mu_s 0.3 mu_k 0.2, released from rest. At t = 0.2 s: acceleration of the 4 kg block, tension. Time string goes slack? Time the 4 kg block stops?
